title: Lewis Chase reports to Air Force headquarters and Condon
summary: Robert Salas tells of Lewis Chase reports to Air Force headquarters and Condon, about March 1967 at Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana, and reads it from an official document. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Um and so, uh Chase decides he needs to report all this. Um, and he does in a a telegram to Air Force headquarters and also reports to Edward Condan.

plain: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, says that in March 1967 at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a base that held nuclear missiles, an officer named Lewis Chase decided he had to report what had happened there during the UFO events Salas describes. According to Salas, Chase sent a telegram to Air Force headquarters and also reported to Edward Condon, the scientist who led an Air Force funded study of UFOs. If so, it would mean the incident was officially passed up the chain at the time.
